summary: Frontend-only retest of merged 0-360 polar angle overlay + visfAtlas. visfAtlas, color bar, PolarAngleDisc legend, MNI152 base, and dashboard load all PASS. POLAR ANGLE RED FLOOD BUG IS NOT FIXED — coronal, sagittal, and 3D render are completely flooded red when Polar Angle (0-360 deg) is toggled, while only the axial pane shows correct polar-angle colors on cortex with MNI152 base visible beneath. Both hemispheres ARE colored on axial (LH/right hemifield + RH/left hemifield), so the merged 0..360 volume itself is correct. The RCA is in the polar_angle_360 colormap registration in NiivueViewer.jsx — alpha is hard-coded to 255 for all 256 LUT entries, so niivue does NOT treat below-cal_min voxels as transparent. Combined with niivue's trilinear interpolation between a value=1 cortical voxel and a value=0 background voxel, the in-between fragments and the value=0 fragments themselves get mapped to LUT[0] = red instead of being hidden, producing the red flood that fills the brain volume on all three non-axial views.

action_items: FIX RED FLOOD in /app/frontend/src/components/NiivueViewer.jsx lines 89-119 (polar_angle_360 colormap registration). The LUT currently pushes A[i]=255 for ALL 256 indices, so niivue does NOT treat values below cal_min as transparent — it clamps them to LUT[0] = red. Fix: set A[0]=0 (and ideally A[1]=0 also) so niivue's standard cal_min behavior produces a transparent below-threshold band, then A[2..255]=255 for the actual gradient. This matches how niivue's built-in colormaps like 'warm' achieve the transparent below-threshold behavior.

Alternative / complementary fix: add `ignoreZeroVoxels: true` to the benson_polar_angle entry in /app/frontend/src/lib/atlasConfig.js. The addOverlayFromUrl helper in NiivueViewer.jsx (lines 278-283) already wires this through correctly. NOTE: this alone may not be sufficient because niivue's trilinear interpolation produces fractional values in (0,1) between cortex (value>=1) and background (value=0), and those fractional values are NOT zero — they would still hit LUT[0]=red. The colormap-alpha fix is the more robust solution.
Optional: set vol.interpolation = 'nearest' for label-like categorical data — but polar angle is continuous so this is not appropriate here.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/components/NiivueViewer.jsx lines 89-119: the polar_angle_360 colormap synthesis hard-codes A.push(255) for every LUT index. This silently breaks cal_min transparency behavior. Either propagate alpha from the stops table (so callers can request a transparent below-threshold ramp) or set A[0]=0 by default.

/app/frontend/src/lib/atlasConfig.js line 48: cal_min=1 is correctly set on benson_polar_angle to hide value=0 background, BUT this only works if the colormap has alpha=0 at its first entry OR ignoreZeroVoxels is set. Neither is true today, hence the red flood. Consider also adding `ignoreZeroVoxels: true` here as defense-in-depth.

/app/frontend/src/components/NiivueViewer.jsx addOverlayFromUrl (lines 249-310): solid implementation — ignoreZeroVoxels, colormapNegative, colormapLabel all wired correctly. Just the colormap-alpha gap above blocks the polar angle path.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro: load dashboard, expand Retinotopy section, click [data-testid=toggle-benson_polar_angle]. Wait ~5-7s for /atlases/benson14_polar_angle.nii.gz load. Inspect the 4 multiplanar panes. EXPECTED: all 4 panes show MNI152 gray base anatomy with polar colors ONLY on cortex (especially occipital). ACTUAL today: only the axial pane (bottom-left) is correct; coronal/sagittal/3D-render are flooded red across the whole brain volume. The benson14_polar_angle.nii.gz file itself is correct (verified via nibabel-equivalent numpy parse: shape=207x256x215, datatype=float32, value range 0..359.99, 380341 nonzero voxels of 11.4M total, 184050 in 1..180 (LH), 196291 in 180..360 (RH), 11M+ at exactly 0 for background). So the bug is purely client-side colormap-alpha handling in NiivueViewer.jsx polar_angle_360 registration.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: In /app/frontend/src/components/NiivueViewer.jsx lines 89-118, the polar_angle_360 colormap is registered via nv.addColormap with R/G/B/A/I arrays. The synthesis loop pushes A.push(255) for every one of the 256 entries (line 104). In niivue, the alpha channel of the LUT is what makes cal_min produce a transparent below-threshold band: voxels with value <= cal_min are mapped to LUT index 0, and only become transparent if LUT[0].A is 0. With A=255 throughout, ALL voxels — including value=0 background and interpolated fractional values between background and cortex (which trilinear sampling produces in abundance, especially for the volumetric ray-march of the 3D render and the off-cortex coronal/sagittal slices) — are rendered as the LUT[0] color, which is red (255,0,0). This produces the observed red flood across coronal, sagittal, and 3D render panes. The axial pane happens to look mostly correct because the slice is taken at a Z position deep in the occipital cortex where the volume's non-zero data dominates the visible slab; but even there a faint red tint is visible above the occipital region. MITIGATION (recommended): change line 104 in NiivueViewer.jsx from `A.push(255)` to `A.push(i === 0 ? 0 : 255)` (or A[0]=A[1]=0) so the colormap supplies a transparent below-threshold ramp, restoring niivue's standard cal_min=transparent semantics. Belt-and-suspenders: also set `ignoreZeroVoxels: true` on the benson_polar_angle layer in atlasConfig.js to ensure exact-zero background voxels are dropped before interpolation.
